keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row for the rebel-held north. The First Ivorian Civil War page describes 'a de facto partition' with 'a rebel-held north and a government-held south'; the Forces Nouvelles page names zones centred on Bouna, Katiola, Bouaké, Mankono, Séguéla, Man and Touba. Neither gives the share of the country held or the front line (page silent), so the extent is an admin-1 reading.

ledger.note: 19 September 2002: the northern rebellion takes the north. The war 'began with a military rebellion on 19 September 2002'; the rebels 'quickly established control over much of the north of the country', including Bouaké and Korhogo.

December 2002: the rebel movements form the New Forces. The Forces Nouvelles page: 'a political coalition that was formed in December 2002, in the wake of the first peace accords' of the MPCI, MPIGO and MJP; the MJP 'has folded into the MPCI, and the MPCI stands in for the coalition itself'. The held territory is unchanged.

ledger.note: 2011: the New Forces are absorbed by the state. Page silent on the date the rebel zones ended: the First Ivorian Civil War page gives the 4 March 2007 Ouagadougou peace agreement and the July 2008 dismantling of the UN buffer zone; the Forces Nouvelles page says 'After the New Forces were mostly integrated into the Ivorian army in 2011'. The year is a bridging judgment.

wars.outcome: Ceasefire on 17 October 2002, Linas-Marcoussis Accord on 26 January 2003, comprehensive ceasefire on 3 May 2003 and the Ouagadougou agreement of 4 March 2007; the north stayed rebel-held in a 'de facto partition'.
wars.note: Infobox: 19 September 2002 - 4 March 2007. On 16 April 2007 Gbagbo declared the war over and presided over the first steps to dismantle the UNOCI buffer zone, fully dismantled in July 2008 and replaced by a 'green line'.

wars.name: Second Ivorian Civil War
wars.outcome: 'The second civil war ended with Gbagbo's defeat and arrest in April 2011.' The page gives no territorial division.
wars.note: The Ivory Coast page: 'The 2010 presidential election led to the 2010-2011 Ivorian crisis and the Second Ivorian Civil War.' The part the New Forces played is not on the pages opened.

certainty.note: A rebel zone with a ceasefire line the pages do not describe; the extent is the researcher's admin-1 reading.

notes: Written by the batch af-08-h as a rebel dossier for the rebel-held north that the republic-of-cote-d-ivoire dossier carries as a loss (2002) and a gain (2011). Budget: the three pages are shared with that dossier. Thin on purpose: the pages give no front line, share of the country, rebel capital or end of rebel administration. The 2011 end is confidence 1; a gap-filler should open 'Ivorian Civil War' articles on the 2007-2011 period (Ouagadougou Political Agreement, the 2010 election, the 2011 Battle of Abidjan) and 'Zone of confidence'. The capital Bouaké is the researcher's reading of 'stronghold'. Whether the Forces Nouvelles deserve a separate colour for nine years or should be drawn as a contested zone is the colour agent's call.
